It's encouraging that he's willing to go to counseling — that's a meaningful sign he hasn't given up, even if his actions feel confusing right now. Many couples go through periods of separation and do find their way back to each other, especially when both people are open to working on things with professional help.

Counseling can give you both a safe space to understand what's driving his need for distance and what you each need moving forward. In the meantime, try to focus on what you can control — taking care of yourself and your kids, being honest about your feelings without pressure, and letting the counseling process unfold. It's okay to feel uncertain; this is a painful and disorienting situation. Try not to interpret his casual demeanor as indifference — people sometimes minimize things around their children to protect them. The fact that you're both still in conversation and he's open to counseling suggests there's something worth working with. Take it one step at a time.
